title: Define attribution for hierarchical KV prefetch + dynamic batch-fusion billing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: when multiple small requests are fused into a single GPU batch at runtime and some of those requests contain hierarchical KV/prefix cache hits (where earlier tokens are satisfied by cache but later tokens require compute), our current metering assigns compute-token costs inconsistently. This causes quota undercharging for fused requests, double-counting for requests that are split, and unpredictable throttling behavior for customers on tight quotas.

Goal: define precise, implementable rules for attributing consumed compute tokens and quota charges across: (a) prefix-only cache hits, (b) partial KV hits inside fused batches, and (c) requests that are dynamically merged or split by the serving runtime. Ensure these rules are deterministic, testable, and can be reconciled in post-hoc billing reports and quota enforcement hooks.
background:
We already have multiple heuristics in the runtime: prefix prefetch, KV-based prefix cache, and an opportunistic batch-fusion path that merges small requests arriving within a microwindow. Prior tickets addressed charging for coalesced batches and partial KV hits, but we observed corner cases when hierarchical prefetch (prefix cache pointing to KV entries that themselves are hierarchical) intersects with on-the-fly fusion. Examples seen in production: 1) a fused batch with 3 requests where request A has a prefix cache hit for tokens 0..20 then needs compute for 21..64, request B is full compute, request C is prefix-only — current metering assigned full compute cost to B and prorated rest incorrectly; 2) quota throttling occurred for request C even though it was served entirely from cache, because the batch's aggregate metering deducted tokens from the customer's quota.

Stakeholders: billing, runtime, quota service, SRE, product (quota semantics), and support (customer disputes).
proposal:
Adopt a two-axis attribution model: (1) token-source classification at runtime (CACHE_READ, KV_PREFIX_HIT, COMPUTE), tracked per-request and per-token; (2) batch-aggregation accounting step that applies deterministic rules to map batch-level compute work back to individual requests. Specific rules: 
- Rule A (cache-only requests): if a request's entire response tokens are satisfied by prefix/KV cache, charge zero compute tokens and do not consume quota for compute units; still mark a lightweight cache-read metric for observability (cache_reads).
- Rule B (partial-cache requests): if a request has some tokens from cache and some requiring compute, charge compute tokens only for the compute portion. When a fused batch mixes partial and full-compute requests, compute costs are first attributed proportional to each request's compute-token count.
- Rule C (batch fusion overhead): introduce a small fixed per-batch overhead (BATCH_BASE) to attribute shared kernel work (e.g., context setup). Overhead is allocated proportionally by compute-token shares among non-cache tokens.
- Rule D (prefetch KV hierarchical hits): hierarchical KV matches that avoid compute should be treated as cache-only for attribution; however, when hierarchical prefetch results are stale and lead to a fallback compute, the original cache read should be credited back in reconciliation and any temporary quota deduction reversed with an audit log entry.
- Rule E (quota enforcement hooks): quota checks should consider estimated compute before fusion (sum of per-request worst-case compute tokens) and also the post-fusion definitive compute attribution. Enforcement should only throttle if post-fusion attribution exceeds quota; transient pre-fusion reservations may be used to avoid oversubscription but must be reconciled within 60s to avoid customer-visible charges.

Implementation pieces: runtime will emit per-request per-token annotations in the batch metadata stream. A new accounting microservice (metering-worker) will consume batch-level annotations and apply Rules A-E to generate final charge events and quota deltas. Reconciliation job will compare provisional quota reservations with final attribution and emit corrections.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for token-source classifier with synthetic hierarchies show 100% deterministic labels for CACHE_READ/KV_PREFIX_HIT/COMPUTE
Integration test: 50k simulated mixed batches where batch-fusion merges varying mixes; final per-request compute tokens match golden-reference allocator within 0.1%
Canary in production on staging tenant group for 48h without >0.5% delta in billed compute compared to offline simulation
Quota enforcement: no cache-only request ever triggers compute quota decrement in canary group
Reconciliation job demonstrates correct reversal of provisional reservations within 60s for 99.9% of cases
Dashboard panel added showing: per-batch BATCH_BASE, per-request compute attribution, mismatch rate between provisional and final charges
test_plan: Add token-level annotation unit tests in runtime repo (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123)
Create synthetic load harness in chaos/bench (script: gs://redwood-drive/bench/fusion-metering-harness) to generate mixed cache/compute patterns
Run integration on staging with deliberate stale-KV cases to validate reconciliation kicks in and reverses provisional charges
Introduce GKE job for metering-worker in canary namespace and observe metrics for 48h
Manual validation steps for support: run sample transcript for disputed calls and compare provisional vs final charge logs
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime annotations (runtime PR) behind feature flag 'annotate_token_source'
2) Deploy metering-worker in canary tenant group (10% of non-enterprise traffic), enable final attribution but keep provisional reservations active
3) Monitor billing dashboards and 'provisional_vs_final_mismatch' alert for 24-72h
4) If mismatch <0.5% and no customer complaints, expand to 50% and run 7 days
5) Flip feature flag to default on for all and deprecate provisional-only path after 30 days of final-attribution stability
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff sync with billing and runtime teams. Agreed on two-axis model (token-source + batch allocator). Action: runtime to prototype token annotations.
2026-03-04: PoC completed by Diego: runtime emits per-token tags for a toy model. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123

2026-03-05: Billing requested explicit handling for multi-tenant batches where requests belong to different customers — resolved: attribution is per-request and we will never aggregate cost across tenants; cross-tenant batch overhead allocated per-tenant share.

2026-03-07: Design review with SRE and Quota service. Decided to allow provisional reservations but require reconciliation within 60s. Logged decision in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/KB-1234
2026-03-09: Implemented metering-worker skeleton and end-to-end test harness (branch: feat/metering-mapper). Internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/221
2026-03-10: Discovered edge case where a fused batch contains churned KV entries (evicted mid-batch) — added check to treat eviction during serving as 'fallback compute' and mark for reconciliation
2026-03-12: PM feedback (Maya Singh): require explicit visibility for customers — added dashboard requirement and audit log entries for any reconciliation that reverses charges
2026-03-13: Ready for canary deployment pending runtime PR code review and billing infra quota hook tests. Assigned Diego to shepherd canary.
